entries.en: The front mirror and the wide-angle mirrors no longer disappear and come back while you drag the top view divider in portrait: the front mirror now goes once and stays away until the top view is smaller again, so portrait windows about 660 to 765 px wide can be without it at the default split.
On a portrait screen with a notch at the top, a run with the mirrors only keeps its toast, its goal message and the cockpit label below the notch.
Offline-ready now also waits for the assets of the chosen graphics quality to be downloaded, so choosing High while online makes it work offline.
On a portrait tablet, a run with the mirrors only keeps the gear, the speed and the counters inside the bar at the bottom of the screen, clear of the brief and the speed lever.
The side windows of the Arocs and MAN cabs now end at the B-pillar just behind the driver, as on the real cabs, so the driver sees out beside him and the glass matches the open cockpit.
The mirror-only drive keeps the counters clear of the speed lever on narrow landscape screens, wrapping them below the gear and the speed.

The outside view no longer looks out over bare ground beyond the yard: a neighbouring estate of sheds, offices and poplar rows now surrounds the site, and on Balanced the plots around the yard show their halls, office and trees.

Einweiser mode: on a desktop, the exercise and free yard setup lets you play as the ground guide, who walks the yard in first person and guides a simulated driver with the BG hand signals; the result lists his faults by rule, and Continue and the replay pick up his runs.
A hidden tab or minimised window now opens the pause sheet, so the run no longer carries on at once on return.
The German About screen translates the asset credit labels, and the German steering wheel hint mentions scrolling.
The steering wheel and the speed lever now tell screen readers their name and value, such as "12 % left" and "80 %".
The pause sheet now explains what Finish and Leave without scoring do, and the German Finish button reads "Fahrt werten" instead of "Beenden".

Parked trailers and container chassis in the yard roll on round wheels with rims, and the curtain-siders gain chevrons on the underrun guard, side rails with amber markers, rear lamps and sturdier landing gear.
Trucks and trailers show rounded tyres with a tread, dished rims with studs, brake drums and axles in the mirrors and the outside view on the Balanced and High graphics settings.
Settings now explains the graphics quality choice, the offline status names what to do next, "Ready offline" no longer shows twice, and Controls has the same chevron as other rows.
The title now says up front when the device has no WebGL 2 graphics and what to try, and the Start buttons stay disabled instead of failing after a press.
On High, the vehicles show road grime on their lower body, wheel arches and chassis, and a slight variation in their paint and tarpaulin.
The angle gauge labels no longer break in the middle of a word on small screens.
Side contour markings are white instead of yellow, and truck rims are black with a silver nut ring.
A failure during a run no longer freezes the view silently: the run stops and a notice offers a reload or the way back to the menu.

The trucks look closer to the real THW vehicles in the mirrors and the chase view: a wider light bar, step wells, kit under the chassis, a ladder and black mudguards on the tipper, and a boxy tarpaulin, red and white striped rear posts and single rear tyres on the MAN.
The German coupling and turntable angle labels break with a hyphen on short screens instead of splitting mid-word.
The outside view has a free camera (K or the camera button) that flies anywhere over the yard while you keep driving.

The low-loader looks like the THW original in the mirrors and the outside view: bright blue frame, dark plank deck, galvanised trough covers, boxes and support legs, and taller ramps with perforated treads and red/yellow marker plates; the Lafette's side contour is white like the other vehicles.

Both trucks carry black mirror heads on arms straight out from the A-pillars and a front mirror just ahead of the windscreen, and the side mirrors now sit at the height of the real THW trucks' mirrors, so the main and wide-angle mirrors look from higher up.
Gear and Stop buttons respond to Enter, error notices are announced and focused, the replay timeline reads its time, and Tab stays inside the pause dialog.

The result screen stays clear of the update toast, the target arrow keeps off the view-size divider, the key list calls Space "Stop" like the button, angles read `n°` on the result, and the replay names its exercise.
The menu is a title screen with Exercises, Free yard and Settings, and a run's vehicles, time of day and driving view are chosen on a setup screen before Start.
The title screen has an About screen with the licence of the app, the licences of its libraries and the credits for its textures and sky, readable offline.
A Controls screen, opened from the title or from Settings, lists the drive keys for your graphics quality and driving view and the touch and mouse controls.
Continue on the title starts your last exercise or free yard in one step, with the truck, trailer, time of day and driving view it shows.
The pause sheet has a Settings level where Theme, Wide-angle mirrors and Graphics quality can be changed; changes apply at once.
The cockpit no longer ends half a pixel short of the room its controls need when the top-down view is at its largest.
The render resolution more often returns to full when a heavy scene gives way to a lighter load that lowering it cannot help.
The side mirrors shrink instead of reaching into the on-screen controls on tablet-sized windows with a bottom inset.
In a short portrait cockpit with the key legend open, the toast and goal messages no longer cover the key list.

The Aids and Angles chips show a chevron that points down while their panel is open, the Angles chip is unavailable while the angle display is off, and the toolbar keeps clear of the Stop button in narrow windows.
On a short screen without the top view, the goal cue now steps aside while a warning shows, so neither covers the forward view or the gear buttons.
The headliner no longer covers the left side mirror on near-square portrait windows.
The view control keeps rounded ends on each row when it wraps on a narrow window.
The class II mirror and the wide-angle mirror no longer flip back and forth while you drag the top view divider on a portrait tablet.
Class II mirrors on short windows keep their gap above the controls instead of letting the view frame touch the control labels.
On narrow landscape screens the longest German messages fit beside the stop button and lever, and the long angle words break with a hyphen.
Below 700 px window height the aid legend opens over the top view and closes on your next control input, and the counters stand beside the angle gauges.
The key list on short screens opens clear of the toolbar buttons, the divider and the messages.
The side and wide-angle mirrors no longer cover the view straight ahead: the side mirrors move up or shrink, and the wide-angle mirrors are left out where they would cover it.
Trainer for two trucks and two turntable drawbar trailers (four combinations) with realistic coupling behavior and collisions.
The app with its menu and driving screen.
A yard with a street and five exercises, plus a free yard mode.
Four views (cockpit, two mirrors, top-down) that lower their resolution on weak devices, and a display with angle gauges.
Touch, keyboard and mouse controls, including a speed lever that ramps up on W/S and Up/Down.
Scoring with per-criterion results, bests with and without aids, a result screen, and a top-down replay with a timeline, event markers and speed control.
German and English UI.
Installable offline app with an update prompt, update check, a screen that stays on while driving, an offline status and a notice when the device cannot show the graphics.
Pause sheet with an unscored restart when leaving a run.
Top-down aids: zoom and pan, the predicted path for truck and trailer, a marked slalom turn point, and a contact marker naming the body part.
Clearer exercise goals while driving.

More realistic cockpit and mirror views: vehicle detail, a sky gradient, contact shadows, haze with an industrial skyline, road markings per the German RMS guidelines, a German industrial yard and the remaining yard props.
Loading is retried after a failure, borders are easier to see and the speed lever has a rail.
Graphics quality presets Low, Balanced and High in settings, defaulting to Balanced.
Smoother edges in the mirrors.
Content keeps clear of notches and screen edges, mirrors are bigger and narrow windows lay out correctly; on shorter screens the mirrors stay above the controls.
The desktop key legend is collapsed and the top view panels are slimmer.
Holding W/Up or S/Down ramps the speed lever.
Cockpit, mirrors and top-down are clearly separated, and grounds, obstacles and halls are distinguishable.
The top-down view draws wheels, axles, turntable and drawbar, keeps a dark outline under aid lines, and frames the whole yard and the follow view clear of the display panels.
The steering wheel shows its position and the straight state, and the controls layout is corrected.
The forward view from the cockpit is no longer blocked by opaque cab glass, and the skyline draws a quay crane.
The slalom requires weaving between the obstacles, and exercise order and result details are corrected.
The run clock and the with-aids mark start with the first driving input, and the last moment counts when a run ends in the target.
Result screen comparison to the best, keyboard use and leaving a run unscored are corrected; the keyboard keeps working after the pause sheet closes.
The clock rounds correctly and a double click no longer selects text; the cockpit layout fits 1280-pixel-wide windows, and Stop no longer covers the counters at 1024x700.
Detailed kerbs, precast walls, loading ramps and traffic-red cones in the cockpit and mirror views.
An outside view orbits the truck to show its cab, with drag to turn and wheel to zoom; it is not offered on the Low graphics preset.
THW-blue cab and body livery for both trucks in the mirrors and outside view, with a crew cab on the MAN and a tipper on the Arocs.
High graphics preset adds a detailed concrete and asphalt ground texture in the cockpit and mirror views.
THW livery for the low-loader and Lafette trailers in the mirrors and outside view.
High graphics preset adds sky reflections on vehicle glass and a satin paint sheen.
Cockpit view gains a cab interior frame (roof header, visor, A-pillars, dashboard edge) on the Balanced and High presets.
Resizable top-down view: drag or use the keyboard on the divider to change its share, saved per orientation.
Top-down path lines now show one matched left/right corridor from the leading end, with a stop bar and a legend explaining every aid.
The THW Kipper and Tieflader look more like the real vehicles, with a low three-way tipper body and a machine transporter with wheel troughs and ramps.
The render resolution no longer drops during startup hitches and recovers on its own once the device keeps up.
When the graphics stop during a run, they restart on their own instead of waiting for the browser.
Edges and thin parts such as fence bars are smoothed slightly differently, and the soft shadow under the vehicles is a little lighter.

Vehicle lamps follow UN R48: headlamps sit in the bumper, the rear clusters lower, and trailers gain drawbar and corner side markers. Only the stop and reversing lamps light so far, while braking and in reverse; the other lamps stay dark until the night mode arrives.
Groundwork for WebGPU graphics on supporting devices; nothing changes for now.
High graphics lights the cockpit, mirror and outside views from a real sky: a photographic cloudy sky that the vehicles reflect, a matching sun and sky light, softer highlights and distance haze.
The cockpit, mirror and outside views draw the yard markings lit on Balanced and High; the top-down view is unchanged.
The cockpit, mirror and outside views draw the target outline, tolerance band and waypoint gate lit on Balanced and High; the top-down view is unchanged.
Stored bests and replays from earlier versions were reset once.
On High, the cockpit, mirror and outside views draw the yard, street and pavement as photoscanned concrete, asphalt and pavers, with slab joints on the yard.
High graphics preset adds sun shadows from the vehicles and yard props in the cockpit, mirror and outside views.
On High, the ground is darker beside obstacles and props and shows tyre scuffs, oil drips, manholes and gully gratings on the yard and street.
The High graphics preset draws the yard's surroundings: halls, an office with flagpoles, a wash canopy, hedges, street trees and benches around the yard and street.
The High graphics preset draws the yard's painted markings worn in the cockpit, mirror and outside views, with every edge kept intact.
The cab windows no longer cast a false sun shadow on High, which keeps the cab interior lit.
Stored runs for both yards are reset once: street furniture beside the hall walls and gatehouse, the entrance sign posts and the plot fences along the street are now solid.
The driver now sits at the left seat of the cab instead of near the centre, so the cockpit view starts from the left.

The cockpit view now matches the left-hand seat: a wide left and a slim right windscreen pillar, a dashboard that dips towards the windscreen centre with an instrument hump straight ahead, and the sun visor over the driver.
The menu has a What's new screen that lists recent changes.
The cockpit eye now sits above the windscreen sill, so the view looks out over the dashboard line instead of through its lower edge.
Buildings, trees, fences and other yard surroundings now cast the sun's shadow on High.
The What's new menu entry shows a "New" badge and lists unseen changes first under "Since your last visit".
On High graphics the cockpit shows a three-dimensional cab interior with a dashboard, door tops and steering wheel in place of the flat overlay.
The cab interior on High graphics is now lit by the sun and sky and shaded by the cab roof.
The menu has a Day/Night choice: night drives show the yard after dark, keep their own bests and replay at night.
The target outline has a dark edge so it stands out on the yard.
Lights and hazard lights switch with H and X or the new buttons under the gears.
At night on Balanced and High graphics, the headlights light the yard ahead and the reversing lamps light the ground behind truck and trailer.
At night, cones, posts and barriers shine in the headlights, side markers glow and the dashboard instruments light up.
At night on High, the headlamp beam and the trailer's rear light now cast shadows.
At night, the yard floodlights light the yard, street lamps throw warm pools on the road and the lamp heads glow.
At night, work floodlights on the truck body and on the trailer's rear come on when you reverse with the lights on, lighting the drawbar gap and the ground behind the trailer.
At night on High, two of the yard's floodlight masts cast shadows of the props across the yard.
Side marker lamps on the truck and trailers flash with the direction indicators when the hazard lights are on, as UN R48 allows.
The top-down view at night is darker, so the yard reads like a night yard while every target and marking stays readable.
Trucks and trailers now show a white lamp facing forward at each rear top corner, visible in both main mirrors at night, as UN R48 allows.
The render resolution stays at full on a device that keeps up, instead of dropping for no reason.
A front mirror at the top of the windscreen shows the ground ahead of the bumper, which the dash hides.
Wide-angle mirrors under the side mirrors show the ground beside the truck and the trailer swinging out.
A "Wide-angle mirrors" setting in the menu hides them and gives the main mirrors their full size back.
The wide-angle mirrors now show on laptop screens, with the main mirrors a little smaller to make room.
Straight reverse now starts with the combination slightly bent, so the trailer drifts off the line unless you correct it.
Night headlights now light the ground in front of each lamp, as two beams that merge further ahead, instead of one beam from between them.
At night, about a quarter of the office windows in the distant skyline glow warm on Balanced and High.
On short screens the warning and goal messages now stand between the side mirrors, or in the top view where they do not fit, instead of covering the cockpit label and the mirrors.
The outside view can be turned and tilted freely around the whole vehicle with drag, pinch, wheel or the keys `,` `.` `PgUp` `PgDn`, and `0` returns to the default view.
On High graphics the cockpit view can be looked around in by dragging with a finger or the mouse, or by holding `Q` or `E` to glance to a side; the view eases back on release.
On a device that is slow for reasons lowering the resolution cannot fix, the picture no longer drops to the lowest resolution and stays there.
A close-proximity mirror above the passenger-side mirror shows the ground right beside the cab on large windows.
The replay starts at the first driving input instead of idle time before it, and the steering readout shows no arrow at 0 %.
Wheel arches and mudguards shade smoothly, and the High-quality yard trees load faster.
The blocked toast is clearer, a limit stop ahead now warns, and the top-right button is labelled Pause.
On short screens the key list opens to the drive keys only, which leaves the mirrors their size; the Keys toggle opens the full list.
High graphics loads its ground textures from a much smaller download, so the first High start is faster.
The menu lists the numbered exercises first, with the vehicle and time of day below, and the free-yard cards describe themselves.
On a night drive with the System theme, the HUD and on-screen controls use the dark look; an explicit Light or Dark theme still wins.
The goal cue near the target now shows the distance and whether the angle is ok, and the result title has a colour and an icon.
The result screen is now announced by screen readers with its outcome when it opens.
In languages other than English, What's new shows a note that its entries are in English.
The view reset button has its own recentre icon, and selected toolbar toggles are now filled with the accent colour so the pressed state reads clearly in light and dark themes.
Below 700 px screen height the exercise brief collapses on the first drive input and the key legend opens as an overlay, leaving more of the top view and the cockpit free.
A "Driving view" choice in the menu drives a run with the mirrors only: the cockpit fills the window without the top view, the brief and counters stay on screen, and the run is ranked apart.

The view buttons are now one joined control with the selected view filled, aid and panel toggles are rounded chips with a lighter tint and a ticked ring, and the replay play button is a pill so it no longer looks like a selected option.
The menu and the What's new screen show the app version, or the build for a development build.
